At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Resolute Mind:
"This is the Devaputra Manifested Mind!
He has come here from the world-system of Abhirati, the realm of the Buddha Akṣobhya; in that place, this person constantly expounds the Śūraṅgama Samādhi."
Dṛḍhamati! There is not a single Buddha who does not speak of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi. Dṛḍhamati!

This Devaputra Manifest Mind shall attain Buddhahood in this Sahā world; desiring to sever these five turbidities and evils, he has come here to take hold of a pure Buddha-field to teach and transform sentient beings, and to cultivate and increase the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
Dṛḍhamati addressed the Buddha, saying:
"In how much time will this son of heaven attain the path of Buddhahood in this world-system?
What shall his name be?"
"What is the name of this world?

The Buddha said, "After these thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa have passed into extinction, there will be no further Buddhas for sixty-two kalpas. During that interval, only hundreds of thousands of millions of pratyekabuddhas will appear, and within it, sentient beings will plant roots of goodness."
After this kalpa has passed, he shall attain Buddhahood, named King of Pure Light Renown Tathāgata.
At that time, the world shall be called Pure Vision.

Then, the Tathāgata King of Pure Light Renown will be able to cause the minds of sentient beings to become pure; the beings of that world shall not be shrouded by greed, hatred, or delusion, but shall attain pure faith in the Dharma and all practice wholesome dharmas.

Dṛḍhamati! The lifespan of this Buddha King Renowned Pure Light was ten minor kalpas; he delivered sentient beings by means of the Dharma of the three vehicles. Among them, immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas attained the Śūraṅgama Samādhi and achieved mastery over all dharmas.
At that time, both Māra and his followers all practiced the Mahāyāna, cultivating compassion for sentient beings.
That Buddha-land was free from the three evil realms and all places of hardship; it was adorned and pure like Uttarakuru, devoid of demonic activities and liberated from all false views.
After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, the Dharma shall remain for ten million billion years.
Resolute Mind!
This son of heaven shall attain the Way of the Buddha in such a pure land.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Resolute Mind said to the devaputra,
"You have attained great benefit, for the Tathāgata has bestowed upon you the prediction of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
The devaputra replied: "Good son!
If there is nothing to be attained regarding any dharma, this is called the great benefit; to have attainment regarding dharmas is to have no benefit."
"Good son! Therefore, you should know that if one does not grasp at dharmas, this is called the great benefit.
When this Dharma was spoken, twenty-five thousand devaputras—who had planted many roots of merit in previous lives—all resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Ten thousand bodhisattvas attained the patience of non-arising.

At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One! This is unprecedented!
Now that you preach the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, these evil Māras do not come to disturb us."
The Buddha said to Śāriputra,
“Do you wish to see the misfortunes and afflictions of Māra?
“Indeed, I wish to see them.”

At that time, the Buddha emitted from the white tuft between his eyebrows a light of the Great Man’s mark, whereby the entire assembly saw the evil Māra bound with fivefold fetters, unable to free himself.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra,
“Do you see the evil Māra bound by the five fetters?
“Indeed, I see him,” he replied.
“By whom is this evil Māra bound?
The Buddha replied,
“It is by the majestic spiritual power of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.”

In whatever Buddha-land one preaches the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, if any māras therein should wish to create obstacles with evil intent, by the power of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi and the majestic spiritual power of the Buddhas, all those evil māras will see themselves bound with the fivefold fetters.

Śāriputra! In whatever place this Śūraṅgama Samādhi is taught—whether during my present lifetime or after my parinirvāṇa—all the Māras, their followers, and any other people who harbor evil intentions will be bound by the five fetters through the majestic spiritual power of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
At that time, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others in the assembly addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Regarding this samādhi, our minds have no doubt and we shall not create obstacles; we do not wish for our bodies to be bound by the five fetters.”
"Blessed One!
Out of reverence for this samādhi, we shall all go to protect those who preach this Dharma, regarding this samādhi as the Blessed One himself."
The Buddha addressed the devas, nāgas, and spirits:
"For this reason, you should attain liberation from the twelve bonds of views.
What are these twelve?"

The bond of the view of self, the bond of the view of sentient beings, the bond of the view of life-span, the bond of the view of a person, the bond of the view of annihilation, the bond of the view of permanence, the bond of the view of "I act," the bond of the view of "mine," the bond of the view of existence, the bond of the view of non-existence, the bond of the view of "this" and "that," and the bond of the view of all phenomena—these constitute the twelve.
You should know that if there are sentient beings who give rise to thoughts of hatred toward the Buddha-dharma and desire to destroy it, they all abide in these twelve fetters of views.
"If a person has faith and understanding, follows [this teaching], and does not oppose it, they shall attain liberation from these twelve fetters of views.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Did Māra hear the name of this Śūraṅgama Samādhi being preached today?
The Buddha said, "He heard it as well; however, because he is bound, he was unable to come."
Śāriputra said: "Why does the Tathāgata not, by means of his majestic spiritual power, cause Māra not to hear the name of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi being spoken?
The Buddha said:
"Cease, do not speak such words.
Even if worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges were filled with great fires, one should pass through them for the sake of hearing this exposition of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi."

Why is this? If a person merely hears the teaching of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, I say that such a person attains great and wholesome benefit, surpassing even the attainment of the four dhyānas or rebirth in the four Brahma-abodes.
Śāriputra! If an evil Māra were now to hear the name of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, by this cause and condition, he would transcend all demonic activities;
even if he were bound while hearing it, he would likewise attain liberation from these twelve fetters of views.
Therefore, Śāriputra,
even those of evil views and wicked people who have fallen into the net of Māra should hear this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, let alone those with pure minds who joyfully desire to hear it!
At that time, there was a bodhisattva in the assembly named Unstained by Conduct within the Realm of Māra, who addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Indeed, World-Honored One!
I shall now manifest within the realm of Māra and, by means of my sovereign spiritual power, cause Māra to abide in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.”
The Buddha said,
"As you wish. Thereupon,
the Bodhisattva Māragocarānupalipta suddenly vanished from the assembly and appeared in the palace of Māra, where he spoke to the evil Māra:
“Have you not heard the Buddha speak of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, wherein immeasurable sentient beings all resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and thus escape your domain;
and they shall likewise deliver others, causing them also to escape your domain?”
Māra then replied: "I have heard the Buddha speak the name of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi; however, being bound by the five fetters, I am unable to go there.
These are my two hands, my two feet, and my head."
He asked the Evil Māra again, "Who has bound you?
The Māra immediately replied:
"Just as I first conceived the thought of going to disrupt those who were listening to and receiving the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, I was immediately bound by the five fetters.
Then I further reflected:
'The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas possess great majestic power and are difficult to disrupt; if I were to go there, I might well destroy myself. It would be better for me to remain here in this palace.'"
Having formed this thought, he immediately attained liberation from the five bonds.
The Bodhisattva replied:
“In this way, all ordinary worldlings engage in conceptualization and discrimination, grasping at signs through inversion; therefore, they are bound.
The movement of thought and conceptual proliferation—therefore there is bondage;
seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing—therefore there is bondage.
Within this, there is in truth neither one who is bound nor one who is liberated.
Why is this? Because all phenomena are without bondage, being fundamentally liberated;
all phenomena are without liberation, being fundamentally without bondage.
It is the mark of constant liberation, free from delusion.

When the Tathāgata preaches the Dharma through this gateway, if there are sentient beings who understand this meaning and, desiring liberation, apply themselves with diligent and energetic effort, they shall attain liberation from all bonds.

At that time, seven hundred celestial maidens from among the host of Māras scattered divine flowers, powdered incense, unguents, and various necklaces over the Bodhisattva Māragocarānupalipta, and spoke these words:
"When shall we attain liberation within the realm of Māra?"
The Bodhisattva replied,
"If you can remain unbroken by the bonds of Māra, then you shall attain liberation.
[They asked,] "What is meant by the 'bonds of Māra'?"
"It refers to the sixty-two views.
If a person does not destroy these various views, they will attain liberation from the bonds of Māra.
The goddess spoke again:
"What is meant by 'attaining liberation without destroying various views'?
He replied, "All views fundamentally come from nowhere and go nowhere. If one knows that all views have no characteristic of coming or going, one attains liberation from the bonds of Māra."
All views are neither existent nor non-existent; if one does not discriminate between existence and non-existence, one attains liberation from the bonds of Māra.

If there is nothing seen, this is right view. Such right view is neither right nor wrong. If phenomena are neither right nor wrong, neither active nor passive, one then attains liberation from the bonds of Māra.
These various views are neither internal nor external, nor are they in between; if one likewise does not even think of these views, then one attains liberation from the bonds of Māra.
Upon hearing this teaching, seven hundred celestial maidens attained the patience of compliance (*anulomikī kṣānti*) and spoke these words:
"We, too, shall act without defilement within the realm of Māra, and deliver all those bound by Māra."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Unstained by Conduct in the Realm of Māra said to the evil Māra:
"Your various retinues have already resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; what will you do?"
The Evil Māra replied,
“I am bound by five fetters and do not know what to do.
The Bodhisattva replied:
“Since you have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, you shall be liberated from these bonds.
Then, out of compassion for Māra, the goddesses all spoke these words:
“You should resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; do not conceive thoughts of fear regarding that which is secure.”
"Do not conceive the notion of suffering within pleasure;
do not conceive the notion of bondage within liberation.
At that time, Māra the Evil One, conceiving a crafty and crooked mind, spoke these words:
"If you abandon the bodhicitta, I shall then resolve to attain it.
Thereupon, the goddesses, through their skillful means, said to Māra:
"We have all already abandoned this mind; you may now resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
If a single bodhisattva gives rise to the bodhicitta, all bodhisattvas likewise share this same mind.
Why is this? Because the mind is without differentiation; toward all sentient beings, their minds are entirely equal.
At that time, Māra said to the Bodhisattva Māragocarānupalipta:
"I shall now resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; by these roots of goodness, may my bonds be released."
Having spoken these words, he immediately saw his own body released from its bonds.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Māramaṇḍalagatāsaṃkliṣṭa, by means of his supernormal powers, emitted a great radiance and manifested a pure and wondrous body that illuminated the palace of Māra; Māra saw his own body devoid of majestic splendor, appearing like a mass of ink.

At that time, among the host of Māras, there were two hundred celestial maidens who were deeply attached to sensual desire. Seeing that the Bodhisattva’s physical form was upright and handsome, they conceived lustful thoughts and each said:
"If this man will engage with us in amorous affairs, we shall all comply with his instructions."

At that time, this Bodhisattva, knowing that the celestial maidens were ready for deliverance through their past karmic conditions, immediately manifested two hundred devaputras, whose appearance was dignified and handsome, no different from his own;
he also created two hundred jeweled pavilions with latticed canopies, surpassing the palaces of Māra.

All these celestial maidens saw themselves within this precious pavilion; each thought to herself that she was sporting with this Bodhisattva, her aspirations were fulfilled, and her lustful desires subsided. They all gave rise to a profound mind of love and reverence for the Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva immediately preached the Dharma to them according to their respective needs, and they all resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Then, the Bodhisattva Māragocarānupalipta addressed the Evil Māra, saying:
"You should go to the Buddha."
The Māra thought to himself:
"My bonds have now been loosened; I shall go to where the Buddha is to disrupt his teaching.
At that time, the evil Māra, surrounded by his retinue, went to where the Buddha was and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Please do not speak further of this Śūraṅgama Samādhi. Why is this? Because—”
"As soon as this samādhi was spoken, my body was immediately bound with the fivefold bonds; I only pray that the Tathāgata will further explain other matters.
Then, the Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati said to the evil Māra, "Who shall untie your bonds?"
He replied, "The Bodhisattva Mārgacaryāsaṃkliṣṭa has released my bonds.
[The other asked,] "What did you promise that you have obtained release from your bonds?"
The Māra said,
"I grant that you have resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati:
"Now this evil Māra has generated the thought of enlightenment for the sake of being released from his bonds; it is not with a pure intention.
It is thus, Resolute Mind!"
After my parinirvāṇa, during the final five hundred years, there will be many bhikṣus who resolve upon bodhicitta for the sake of gain and offerings, rather than with a pure intention.
Resolute Mind!
Observe the power of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi and the majestic spiritual authority of the Buddha-dharma.

These bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās, though they may have acted with a frivolous mind, a mind greedy for gain and offerings, or a mind that merely followed after others when hearing of this samādhi, have nonetheless given rise to the bodhicitta.

I know that all these minds can serve as the causal conditions for attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; how much more so when one hears this Śūraṅgama Samādhi and is able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* with a pure mind?
"You should know that this person has already attained definitive certainty within the Buddha-dharma.
The Bodhisattva Resolute Mind addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"

Now, when this evil Māra hears the exposition of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, will he, for the sake of being liberated from his bonds, resolve upon Bodhicitta and likewise attain the complete causes and conditions for the Buddha-dharma?
The Buddha said: "It is as you have said.

By virtue of these causes and conditions of the merit of this samādhi, and by virtue of the cause and condition of having resolved upon bodhicitta, in future lives that evil Māra shall be able to abandon all demonic affairs, demonic conduct, the demonic mind of crookedness, and all demonic afflictions."
"From this day forward, you shall gradually attain the power of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi and achieve the Buddha-way.
The Bodhisattva Resolute Mind said to the evil Māra:
"The Tathāgata has now bestowed a prediction of enlightenment upon you."
The Māra said:
"O son of good family!
Since I have not now generated the aspiration for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* with a pure mind, why has the Tathāgata bestowed a prediction of enlightenment upon me?"
As the Buddha has said:
"From the mind there is karma; from karma there is retribution.
Since I myself have had no intention to seek the path to Bodhi, for what reason has the Tathāgata bestowed this prediction upon me?
At that time, wishing to sever the doubts of the assembly, the Buddha addressed Resolute Mind, saying:
"There are four kinds of predictions for bodhisattvas. What are these four?"

There are those who receive a prediction of enlightenment before they have yet resolved their minds; there are those who receive a prediction at the very moment they resolve their minds; there are those who receive a secret prediction; and there are those who receive a manifest prediction upon attaining the patience of the non-arising of dharmas—these are called the four.
"Only the Tathāgata can know this matter; it is beyond the knowledge of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
'Firm Mind! What is meant by bestowing a prediction of enlightenment upon one who has not yet resolved their mind?"

There may be sentient beings who wander through the five realms—whether in hell, as animals, as hungry ghosts, in the heavens, or among humans—who possess sharp and keen faculties and delight in the Great Dharma.
The Buddha knows that such persons, after the passing of several hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, shall give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;

and furthermore, for several hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, they shall practice the bodhisattva path, making offerings to several hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *nayuta* Buddhas, and transforming and teaching several hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of immeasurable sentient beings, causing them to abide in Bodhi.

Furthermore, after the passage of several hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; your name shall be such, your buddha-field shall be such, the number of your śrāvaka assembly and your lifespan shall be such, and the duration of the Dharma after your parinirvāṇa shall be for as many years as this.
The Buddha said to Resolute Mind:
“The Tathāgata fully understands this matter, and even more than this; this is called bestowing a prediction of enlightenment upon one who has not yet resolved his mind toward awakening.
At that time, the Elder Mahākāśyapa came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"From this day forward, we shall regard all sentient beings as the World-Honored One. Why is this?
We do not possess such wisdom as to know which sentient beings possess the faculties of a bodhisattva."
"Which sentient beings lack the roots of a bodhisattva?
World-Honored One!
Because we do not know such matters, we might give rise to a mind of contempt toward sentient beings, which would be to our own detriment."
The Buddha said: “Excellent! Excellent!”
Kāśyapa! Well said these words.
For this reason, I have stated in my sūtras:
"A person should not recklessly judge sentient beings. Why is this?
If one recklessly judges other sentient beings, one brings harm upon oneself.
Only the Tathāgata is truly such!
He is equal to sentient beings and equal to those who are his peers. For this reason, all śrāvakas and other bodhisattvas should conceive the thought of the Buddha toward all sentient beings.

"Regarding those who have just aroused the mind [of enlightenment] and received a prediction: there may be some individuals who, having long planted the roots of virtue and cultivated wholesome practices, are diligent and energetic, possess sharp faculties, delight in the Great Dharma, and possess great compassion, seeking the path to liberation for all sentient beings."

When such a person resolves their mind [on enlightenment], they immediately abide in *avaivartika* (non-retrogression), enter the rank of bodhisattvas, fall within the number of those destined for certainty, and transcend the eight difficulties.

As soon as such persons resolve their minds, all Buddhas immediately bestow upon them the prediction (*vyākaraṇa*) of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, declaring: "Their name shall be such, their buddha-field shall be such, and their lifespan shall be such."

Regarding such individuals, the Tathāgata, knowing their minds, bestows upon them the prediction [of enlightenment]; this is called "bestowing the prediction at the very moment of generating the resolve.
As for the "secretly bestowed prediction," there are bodhisattvas who, though they have not yet received a prediction, constantly apply themselves with diligence in seeking anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
They delight in various kinds of giving and delight in universal giving;
they are firm in receiving the Dharma and maintain their precepts without forsaking them;
they deeply cultivate adornment, possess the power of great patience, and regard all sentient beings with an impartial mind.
Diligently practicing with vigor, they seek all wholesome dharmas; their bodies and minds are tireless, as if extinguishing a fire on their heads.
Their conduct is mindful and serene, enabling them to attain the four dhyānas;
they joyfully seek wisdom and practice the Bodhi of the Buddhas.
Having long practiced the six perfections, he manifested the signs of attaining Buddhahood.
At that time, other bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others all thought to themselves:
"Such a bodhisattva, with such diligent and vigorous application, is truly rare; when will he attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?"
What is his title? What is the name of his land?
And how great is the number of his assembly of śrāvakas?

In order to sever the doubts of these sentient beings, the Buddha bestowed upon them a prophecy, so that the entire assembly might hear and know it, yet this bodhisattva alone was not permitted to hear it.
By the spiritual power of the Buddha, he caused the entire assembly to know that this bodhisattva would attain buddhahood with such a name, such a land, and such a number of śrāvaka followers.

Whatever the assembly doubted was entirely resolved at that time; they conceived the thought of regarding this bodhisattva as a World-Honored One, yet this bodhisattva could not know for himself whether he had received the prediction or not—this is what is meant by a bodhisattva receiving a prediction in secret.

“Regarding those who receive the prediction in the presence [of the Buddha]: there are bodhisattvas who have long accumulated roots of goodness, such that nothing remains unseen or unattained; they constantly practice the pure conduct, contemplate non-self and emptiness, and attain the patience of the non-arising of all phenomena.”

The Buddha, knowing that this person was already fully endowed with merit and wisdom, bestowed a prophecy in the presence of the great assembly of devas, humans, māras, brahmās, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas, saying:
"O son of good family!..."

After the passing of several hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, you shall attain Buddhahood; your name shall be such, your land shall be such, the number of your śrāvaka assembly shall be such, and your lifespan shall be such.
At that time, countless people followed his example and all resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Having received their predictions of enlightenment before the Buddha, this person ascended into the air to a height of seven *tāla* trees.
“Dṛḍhamati! This is called the fourth ‘face-to-face prediction.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Is there, within this assembly, any bodhisattva who has received the prediction of enlightenment by means of these four matters?
The Buddha replied, “There is.”
“World-Honored One! Who is this?
The Buddha said:

"This Bodhisattva Siṃhanādara-rāja and the householder’s son Rataśrī have received their predictions of enlightenment despite not yet having generated the aspiration for awakening; likewise, countless other bodhisattvas from worlds in the ten directions have also received their predictions without yet having generated the aspiration."

Furthermore, there were the Bodhisattva Śānta, the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the Dharma-Prince Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, and such immeasurable multitudes of bodhisattvas as these; at the very moment they first resolved their minds [on enlightenment], they were all granted predictions of future buddhahood and dwelt within the stage of avaivartika.
Within this assembly, there were also the Bodhisattvas Jñānavīra and Hitamati, as well as immeasurable other bodhisattvas such as these, who were secretly granted predictions of enlightenment.
"Sthiramati!..."

“I and Maitreya, along with the thousand bodhisattvas of the Bhadrakalpa, have all attained the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti) and have received our predictions in the presence of the Buddha.
The Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is rare, World-Honored One!”

The conduct of a bodhisattva is inconceivable, and their reception of the prediction of enlightenment is likewise inconceivable; even all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas cannot know this, let alone other sentient beings.
The Buddha said, “Dṛḍhamati! The conduct,
the exertion of vigor, and the majestic power of a bodhisattva are inconceivable.”

At that time, the goddesses who had been transformed by the Bodhisattva Māragocarānupalipta and inspired to seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi each scattered celestial flowers over the Buddha and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!...”

We do not delight in receiving a prediction in secret; we wish to attain the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) and receive our prediction in the presence [of the Buddha].
We only pray that the World-Honored One will now grant us the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Buddha then smiled, and from his mouth issued various kinds of wondrously colored light that illuminated all the worlds before returning to enter through the crown of his head.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"For what reason do you smile?
The Buddha told Ānanda,
"Do you now see these two hundred goddesses who, with palms joined, pay respectful homage to the Tathāgata?"
“I have seen it, World-Honored One. “Ānanda!
"O celestial maidens!

You have already planted deep roots of goodness in the presence of five hundred Buddhas in the past. From this point forward, you shall again make offerings to countless Buddhas; after seven hundred *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas have passed, you shall all attain Buddhahood, and your title shall be King of Purity (*Viśuddharāja*)."

Ānanda! After these goddesses have ended their lives, they shall all transform their female bodies and be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven, where they will make offerings to and serve Maitreya Bodhisattva!
At that time, having heard that the celestial maidens had received their predictions, Māra the Evil One addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Even I now lack mastery over my own retinue because of hearing this Śūraṅgama Samādhi being preached; how much more so for others who hear it?"
"If anyone hears of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, they will immediately attain definitive certainty and abide within the Buddha-dharma.
At that time, the goddess, with a fearless mind, said to the Evil Māra:
"Do not grieve so greatly; we shall not leave your realm now."

Why is this? The suchness of the realm of Māra is identical to the suchness of the realm of the Buddha; the suchness of the realm of Māra and the suchness of the realm of the Buddha are neither two nor distinct, and we do not depart from this suchness.

The characteristics of the realm of Māra are themselves the characteristics of the realm of the Buddha; the dharmas of the realm of Māra and the dharmas of the realm of the Buddha are neither two nor distinct. We do not go beyond, nor do we transcend, these characteristics of phenomena.

In the realm of Māra there is no fixed dharma that can be pointed out, and in the realm of the Buddha there is likewise no fixed dharma that can be pointed out. The realm of Māra and the realm of the Buddha are neither two nor distinct; we do not emerge from nor transcend these characteristics of dharmas.
Therefore, one should know that all phenomena lack any fixed determination.
Because they lack fixed determination, there is neither "retinue" nor "non-retinue."
At that time, the evil Māra was filled with sorrow and distress, desiring to return to the heavens.
The Bodhisattva Māradharṣaka, who practices within the realm of Māra without being defiled, addressed the evil Māra, saying:
"Where do you wish to go?"
Māra said, "I now wish to return to my own abiding palace.
The Bodhisattva said to him:
"Not departing from this assembly is itself your palace.
At that moment, the evil Māra saw himself situated within his own original palace.
The Bodhisattva said to him:
"What do you see? The evil Māra replied,
"I see myself dwelling in my own original palace, with its beautiful groves, gardens, and ponds— all of which are my own possession."
The Bodhisattva said:
"Can you now offer this to the Tathāgata?
Māra replied:
"So be it! As soon as these words were spoken, he immediately saw the Tathāgata, the śrāvakas, the bodhisattvas, and the entire great assembly, all within that space, preaching the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Between these two donors—the one at whose dwelling the Buddha preached the Śūraṅgama Samādhi and the one who provided the food after which the Buddha attained enlightenment—which one possesses greater merit?”
The Buddha said:

“Ānanda! Whether one gives food to the Buddha after he has already attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, or after he has already turned the wheel of Dharma, or after he has already preached the Śūraṅgama Samādhi—there is no difference in the merit of these three kinds of offerings.”

Ānanda! You should know that wherever I attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, that place is itself vajra. All Buddhas of the past, future, and present have all attained the Buddha-way therein; wherever they dwell, they preach the Śūraṅgama Samādhi without any distinction, and it is likewise so for any place where it is read, recited, copied, or written!
Ānanda! After giving food to the Buddha, he first turned the wheel of Dharma.
If there is a Dharma master who, having received the gift of food, recites and preaches this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, the merit of these two acts of giving is equal and without distinction.
Furthermore, Ānanda!
When the Buddha dwells in a vihāra, he delivers sentient beings through eighteen kinds of supernatural transformations;
yet there may be another vihāra where one recites and expounds this Śūraṅgama Samādhi. The merit of these two places of giving is no different.
At that time, Ānanda said to Māra:
"You have gained great benefit, for you were able to offer your palace to the Buddha so that he might dwell therein. Māra said:
"This is due to the power of the grace of the Bodhisattva Unstained by Conduct in the Realm of Māra.
The Bodhisattva Resolute Mind addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“Is it because the Bodhisattva Māragocarānupalipta dwells in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi that his sovereign spiritual power is thus?
The Buddha said, “Firm Mind! [It is so.]”

As you have said, this bodhisattva now dwells in this samādhi; he is able to manifest all things at will through his supernormal powers, performing the deeds of Māra’s realm without being defiled by those demonic practices, and appearing to enjoy himself with celestial maidens while remaining truly free from the evil dharma of lust.
"O son of good family!
Abiding in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, he manifests entry into the palaces of Māra while his body does not depart from the assembly of the Buddha.
He manifests engaging in the playful diversions of the realm of Māra, yet he transforms sentient beings through the Buddha-dharma."
The Bodhisattva Resolute Mind addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Abiding in this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, how many kinds of sovereign spiritual powers can the Tathāgata manifest?”
“Excellent, World-Honored One!
We pray that you will briefly expound upon this. The Buddha said:

“Dṛḍhamati! I now abide here in this Śūraṅgama Samādhi. Within this trichiliocosm—consisting of ten billion sets of four continents, ten billion suns and moons, ten billion abodes of the Four Heavenly Kings, ten billion Trāyastriṃśa heavens, ten billion Yāma heavens, ten billion Tuṣita heavens, ten billion Nirmāṇarati heavens, ten billion Paranirmita-vaśavartin heavens, up to ten billion Akaniṣṭha heavens, ten billion Sumeru kings of mountains, and ten billion great oceans—this is what is called a trichiliocosm.”
Dṛḍhamati! Abiding in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, within this trichiliocosm, I may manifest the practice of the dāna-pāramitā in Jambudvīpa;
or I may manifest the practice of the śīla-pāramitā in Jambudvīpa.
Or they manifest the practice of the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā) in Jambudvīpa;
or they manifest the practice of the perfection of vigor (vīrya-pāramitā) in Jambudvīpa;
or they manifest the practice of the perfection of meditation (dhyāna-pāramitā) in Jambudvīpa.
Or they manifest the practice of the *prajñāpāramitā* in Jambudvīpa;
or they manifest as five-fold transcendent sages (*pañcābhijña-ṛṣi*) in Jambudvīpa;
or they manifest living as householders in Jambudvīpa.
In some cases, they manifest as renunciants within Jambudvīpa;
in others, they dwell in the Tuṣita Heaven as those destined for one more birth before attaining Buddhahood across the four continents;
and in still others, they manifest as universal wheel-turning monarchs (cakravartin) throughout the four continents.
Some become Śakra-devānām-indra;
some become Brahmā-rājas;
and some become Catur-mahārājas.
Some become kings of the Yāma Heaven;
some become kings of the Tuṣita Heaven;
some become kings of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven.
Sometimes he becomes the king of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven;
sometimes he manifests as a householder;
or he manifests as a lay devotee.
Or again, they may manifest as minor kings or great kings;
or as kṣatriyas; or as brahmins.
Sometimes he acts as a caravan leader;
sometimes, among the four continents, wishing to descend from Tuṣita Heaven to be born into the world,
he manifests entry into a womb.
Sometimes he manifests dwelling in the womb;
sometimes he manifests being about to be born;
or having manifested birth, he walks seven steps and raises his hand, declaring of himself:
"Whether in heaven or on earth, I alone am the most honored!
At times he manifests dwelling in a palace together with court ladies;
at other times he manifests leaving the household life.
In some instances he manifests ascetic practices;
in others he manifests the gathering of grass;
and in others he manifests sitting at the site of enlightenment.
Sometimes he manifests the subduing of Māra;
sometimes he manifests the attainment of Buddhahood;
sometimes he manifests the contemplation beneath the King of Trees.
Some manifest being entreated by Śakra and Brahmā to turn the wheel of Dharma;
some manifest turning the wheel of Dharma;
some manifest relinquishing their life-span.
Sometimes they manifest entry into parinirvāṇa;
sometimes they manifest the cremation of the body;
or they manifest the preservation of the entire body as śarīra relics.
Sometimes he manifests the dispersal of his bodily relics;
sometimes he manifests that the Dharma is about to perish;
or sometimes he manifests that the Dharma has already perished.
In some cases, he manifests an immeasurable lifespan;
in others, he manifests a short lifespan;
and in others, he manifests a land where even the names of the evil realms do not exist.
Sometimes they manifest the various evil realms;
sometimes they manifest Jambudvīpa as pure and adorned like a celestial palace;
and sometimes they manifest it as wretched and evil.
Or they manifest as superior, middling, or inferior. "Firm Mind!

All these are the sovereign spiritual powers of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi. Although Bodhisattvas manifest entry into nirvana, they do not undergo ultimate extinction; yet, within the trichiliocosm, they can manifest such sovereign spiritual powers and display such various adorned phenomena."

Dṛḍhamati! Observe how the Tathāgata turns the wheel of Dharma here in this Jambudvīpa of four continents, while in other Jambudvīpas he has not yet attained the Buddha-way; or in some Jambudvīpas he manifests entry into parinirvāṇa—this is called the dharma-gate entered by the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
At that time, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others in the assembly, as well as the bodhisattvas and great disciples, all had this thought:
"Does Śākyamuni Buddha possess such supernormal power only within this trichiliocosm, or does he also possess such power in other worlds?"
At that time, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, knowing the thoughts of the assembly and wishing to sever their doubts, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

As I have traveled through various buddha-fields, beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of sixty Ganges Rivers in this world-system, there is a buddha-field named Single Lamp Radiance, where a Buddha dwells preaching the Dharma for the sake of beings.”
I went to where he was, prostrated my head at his feet, and asked:
"World-Honored One!
What is your name?"
"How should we uphold the name of that Buddha?
That Buddha replied to me: "Go to Śākyamuni Buddha!"
"I shall answer you myself.
"World-Honored One!
The meritorious adornments of that Buddha-land could not be fully described even in the course of an eon."

Furthermore, it surpasses even this: in that land, there are no names for śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; there is only a community of bodhisattvas who constantly preach the Dharma wheel of non-retrogression.
“I only pray that the World-Honored One will speak of these Buddha-names and of those who preach the Dharma in the land of Single Lamp Radiance!
At that time, the Buddha addressed Mañjuśrī, the Dharma Prince:
“Listen well, all of you; do not harbor fear, nor give rise to doubt or regret.”
Why is this? The spiritual power of all Buddhas is inconceivable, and the power of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi is likewise inconceivable. Mañjuśrī!
The one who expounds the Dharma in that land of Ekadhvajābhyudgata is the Buddha named Sarvaguṇālaṃkāraśrīvyūhaprabhārāja. Mañjuśrī!

In that land of Ekadhvajābhyudgata, the Buddha Sarvaguṇālaṃkāraśrīvyūhaprabhārāja is none other than my own body manifesting the spiritual power of a Buddha in that realm; it is there that I preach the Dharma-wheel of non-retrogression. This is the pure land cultivated by me through my past lives.

Mañjuśrī! You should now know that throughout immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of lands, I possess spiritual power in its entirety, which all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are unable to know.
Mañjuśrī! All of this is the power of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
Bodhisattvas constantly manifest supernatural transformations in immeasurable worlds, yet they do not waver from this samādhi.
Mañjuśrī! It is like the sun and the moon, which do not move from their palaces at all, yet appear in all cities and villages.

In the same way, a bodhisattva abiding in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi does not move at all, yet is able to manifest his body throughout immeasurable worlds, preaching the Dharma according to what sentient beings delight in.

At that time, the assembled multitude attained what they had never experienced before; all were filled with great joy and leaped for immeasurable delight. With palms joined in reverence, they, along with the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others, scattered pearl flowers, various kinds of exquisite blossoms, powdered incense, and unguents over the Buddha.
They all performed every kind of music belonging to the devas as an offering to the Tathāgata and his disciples;
they also each removed their upper garments and presented them to the Buddha, the bodhisattvas, and the rest!
With exquisite flowers as large as Mount Sumeru, along with various incenses, powdered incense, unguents, precious jewels, and necklaces, they scattered them over the Buddha.
They all spoke thus:
"Indeed, World-Honored One!
Wherever the Śūraṅgama Samādhi is taught, that ground shall become adamantine."

If a person hears this samādhi being expounded, accepts it with faith, reads and recites it, and explains it to others without being startled or afraid, one should know that this person is likewise a vajra; they have accomplished indestructible patience, dwell deeply in faith, are protected by all Buddhas, have planted thick roots of goodness, have attained great and excellent benefit, have subdued Māra and his enemies, have severed the paths to the evil realms, and are guarded by spiritual friends.
“World-Honored One!

As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, if there are sentient beings who, upon hearing this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, are able to believe and accept it, read and recite it, explain its meaning, expound it for others, and practice according to the teaching, you should know that such persons have attained a state of certainty within the Buddha-dharma and will never regress.”
The Buddha said: "So it is! So it is!"
It is as you have said.
If a person has not deeply planted various roots of goodness, they will be unable to believe and accept the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
There are few sentient beings who, upon hearing the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, are able to believe and accept it; there are many sentient beings who cannot believe and accept it.
"Good son! There are four dharmas by which a person, upon hearing this samādhi, is able to believe and accept it.
What are these four?

First, having heard this samādhi from various Buddhas of the past; second, being protected by spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) and deeply delighting in the Buddha-way; third, possessing profound roots of goodness and taking pleasure in the Great Dharma; fourth, personally attaining realization of the profound Dharma of the Mahāyāna.
Possessing these four dharmas, one is able to believe in and accept this samādhi. Good son!

Furthermore, there are arhats who have fulfilled their vows, as well as those endowed with right view, those who practice through faith, and those who practice through vision; because such persons follow the words of the Tathāgata, they believe in this samādhi, yet do not personally realize it.
"Why is this? This samādhi cannot be fully penetrated by any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, much less by other sentient beings!
At that time, the Elder Mahākāśyapa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

It is as if a person born blind were to obtain eyes in a dream and see various forms; his heart would be filled with great joy, and within that very dream, he would dwell and converse together with those who possess sight.”
Once this person has awakened, they no longer see forms.
We are just like this!

Before we had heard of this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, our hearts were filled with joy, and we claimed to have attained the divine eye, dwelling and conversing with various bodhisattvas, discussing and expounding upon the principles of the Dharma.
“World-Honored One!
Having now heard of this samādhi from the Buddha, I do not understand its meaning; I am like one born blind, unable to know the dharmas practiced by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.”

From this day forward, we shall regard ourselves as those born blind; regarding the profound Dharma of the Buddha, we possess no wisdom, for we neither know nor see that which the World-Honored One practices.
From this day forward, we know that the Bodhisattvas have truly attained the divine eye and are able to achieve such profound wisdom.
World-Honored One!
If a person lacks the mind of *sarvajñatā* (omniscience), who would dare to claim for themselves:
"I am a wise one; I am a field of merit. The Buddha said, "So it is!"
"So it is! Kāśyapa, it is just as you have said."
"The profound wisdom attained by Bodhisattvas is beyond the reach of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.
When Mahākāśyapa had spoken these words, eight thousand sentient beings all resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Resolute Mind asked the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī, saying: "Mañjuśrī!
Regarding what is called a 'field of merit,' why is it named a field of merit?"
Mañjuśrī said: "There are ten practices of the Dharma that are called fields of merit. What are these ten?"
They abide in the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, yet do not enter the fixed stage of the Dharma;
they perceive and know the Four Noble Truths, yet do not realize the fruits of the Path;
they practice the eight liberations, yet do not abandon the conduct of a bodhisattva.
They are able to give rise to the three types of supernormal knowledge (trividyā) while traversing the triple world;
they can manifest the physical forms and dignified deportment of śrāvakas, yet do not follow their vocal teachings nor seek the Dharma from others;
they manifest the physical forms and dignified deportment of pratyekabuddhas, yet preach the Dharma with unimpeded eloquence (apratihatapratibhāna).
Constantly abiding in meditative concentration while being able to manifest the practice of all activities;
never departing from the right path while appearing to enter false paths;
deeply immersed in craving and attachment yet free from all desires and afflictions.
"Entering into nirvāṇa yet neither destroying nor abandoning saṃsāra—
one who possesses these ten dharmas should be known as a true field of merit.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati asked Subhūti:
“Venerable Subhūti! The World-Honored One has declared you to be the foremost field of merit; do you possess these ten dharmas? Subhūti replied:
"I do not possess even one of these qualities in this Dharma, let alone ten!
Resolute Mind said,
"By what name are you called the foremost field of merit?"
Subhūti said: "I am not the foremost field of merit among the Buddhas and bodhisattvas; the Buddha has declared me to be the foremost field of merit among the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."
"Dṛḍhamati! It is like this: for example, a minor king of a frontier region is also called a 'king';

yet if a Wheel-Turning Sage King arrives in that frontier region, those minor kings are no longer called kings, because at that time there is only the Wheel-Turning Sage King, whose majestic virtue is exceptionally sublime and superior."
Dṛḍhamati! In whatever land, city, or village there may be where no bodhisattvas dwell, I am able to serve as a field of merit therein;
but where there is a Buddha or great bodhisattvas present, I am not called a field of merit therein.
"Because all bodhisattvas possess the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*), they are superior to me.
At that time, the Buddha praised Subhūti, saying: "Excellent!"
Excellent! It is as you have said.
These are the words of a great disciple free from overweening pride!
The Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati again asked the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī:
"Mañjuśrī! Regarding what you have called 'much learning,' why is it named 'much learning'?"

Mañjuśrī said: "If a person hears even a single phrase of the Dharma and immediately understands within it thousands of millions of meanings, and can expound and explain them for hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas with inexhaustible wisdom and eloquence, this is called 'much learning' (bahuśruta)."
Furthermore, Resolute Mind Bodhisattva!
If one hears what is spoken by the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions, one is able to receive and uphold it all;
there is not a single phrase that was not heard before, for everything that is heard has already been heard previously.

They are able to retain whatever Dharma they hear without forgetting it, and they preach it for the sake of sentient beings while realizing there are no sentient beings; thus, there is no distinction between themselves, sentient beings, and the Dharma they preach.
"This is what is called 'being learned'.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva devaputra in the assembly named Viśuddhacandragarbha, who had this thought:
"The Buddha has declared Ānanda to be the foremost among those who are learned. Is Ānanda now truly possessed of such learning as Mañjuśrī has described?"
Having formed this thought, he asked Ānanda:
"The Tathāgata has declared you to be the foremost among those of great learning; does your great learning equal that which Mañjuśrī has described?"
Ānanda replied, "As for the 'great learning' spoken of by Mañjuśrī, I do not possess such a thing.
Vimalacandragarbha said:
“How is it that the Tathāgata always praises you as the foremost among those who are most learned?

Ānanda replied, “Among the Buddha’s disciples who have attained liberation by following after sounds and words, I am said to be the foremost; it does not mean that I am the foremost in learning among the bodhisattvas who possess an immeasurable ocean of wisdom, peerless great intelligence, and unimpeded eloquence.”
"O Son of Heaven!
Just as when there is the light of the sun and moon, the people of Jambudvīpa can see various forms and colors and are able to perform their tasks, so it is with me:

it is solely by means of the light of the Tathāgata’s wisdom that I am able to receive and uphold the Dharma. Within this, I myself possess no power; you should know that all of this is due to the Tathāgata’s spiritual power."
At that time, the World-Honored One praised Ānanda, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"As you have said, you should know that the various dharmas which you uphold, recite, and contemplate are due to the spiritual power of the Tathāgata.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Viśuddhacandragarbha, saying:
"The dharmas upheld by Ānanda are very few; those he does not recite are immeasurable and boundless."
"O Son of Heaven!

Of all the dharmas I have attained at the site of enlightenment, I have not spoken even one part in a hundred thousand billion. And of what I have spoken, Ānanda does not retain even one part in a hundred thousand billion."
"O Son of Heaven!

In a single day and night alone, the Tathāgata preaches the Dharma for the sake of the Śakras, Brahmās, World-Protecting Heavenly Kings, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and other sons of heaven and bodhisattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions."

By the power of wisdom, they compose verses and recite sūtras, nidānas, and parables; they speak of the various pāramitās practiced by sentient beings, as well as the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and the unsurpassed vehicle of the Buddhas. They encompass the Mahāyāna teachings, disparage birth-and-death, and praise nirvāṇa.
"Even if all sentient beings within Jambudvīpa were as accomplished in learning as Ānanda, they would not be able to receive and uphold it in even a hundred thousand kalpas,
O Devaputra!"
"For this reason, you should know that the various dharmas spoken by the Tathāgata are immeasurable and boundless, whereas what Ānanda has retained is but very little!
At that time, the Devaputra Viśuddhacandragarbha immediately offered one hundred thousand flower-canopies made of the seven precious substances to the Tathāgata.
The canopy immediately remained suspended throughout the void, and all sentient beings covered by it were transformed into a golden color.
Having offered the canopy, he spoke these words:
"Indeed, World-Honored One!"
By this merit, may all sentient beings universally possess eloquence in preaching the Dharma just like the World-Honored One,
and be able to receive and uphold the Dharma just like the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī!
At that time, the Buddha, knowing that this Bodhisattva-devaputra deeply delighted in the Buddha-way, conferred upon him the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, saying:
"This devaputra, after four million four hundred thousand kalpas have passed, shall become a Buddha named Ekaratnacchattra."
The name of that land is Adorned with All Manner of Jewels.
When this Dharma was being taught, two hundred bodhisattvas gave rise to a mind of indolence, thinking:

“The Dharma of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, is exceedingly profound; Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi is so difficult to attain that we are unable to fulfill these requirements. It would be better for us simply to enter nirvana by means of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle.”
"Why is this? The Buddha has said that if a bodhisattva should regress, they may become a pratyekabuddha or a śrāvaka.

At that time, Mañjuśrī, the Dharma Prince, knowing that these two hundred bodhisattvas had hearts of indolence and regression, desired to rouse them again so that they might attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; furthermore, wishing to instruct and transform the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others in the assembly, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I recall that in a past kalpa named Illumination, during three hundred and sixty billion lifetimes therein, I entered nirvana by means of the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas.”
At that time, the entire assembly conceived doubts in their hearts:
"If one has entered nirvana, they should not return again to the continuity of birth and death.
Why then does Mañjuśrī now speak these words?"
“World-Honored One!

I recall that in a past kalpa named ‘Illumination,’ during three hundred and sixty billion lifetimes therein, I entered nirvana by means of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle. How is this matter to be understood?
At that time, Śāriputra, receiving the Buddha’s divine intention, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If a person has already attained entry into nirvāṇa, there should no longer be the continuity of birth and death.”
"How is it that Mañjuśrī, having already entered nirvāṇa, is born once again?
The Buddha said, "You may ask him; Mañjuśrī himself shall answer you."
Then Śāriputra asked Mañjuśrī: "If a person has already attained entry into nirvāṇa, they will no longer continue in the succession of existence within the various realms of being."
Why do you now speak these words:
"World-Honored One!

I recall that during the Illuminating Kalpa of the past, across three hundred and sixty billion lifetimes, I entered nirvana by means of the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas"? What is the meaning of this?
Mañjuśrī said: “The Tathāgata exists in the present;
he is the all-knower, the all-seer, the speaker of truth, the one who does not deceive, and one whom no god or human in the world can mislead.”
"What I have spoken, the Buddha himself has realized and known.
If I were to speak otherwise, I would be deceiving the Buddha. Śāriputra!"
At that time, during the eon known as Prabhāsa, a Buddha appeared in the world named Puṣya; having brought benefit to the devas and humans of the world, he entered parinirvāṇa.
After this Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, the Dharma will remain for one hundred thousand years.
After the extinction of the Dharma, among those sentient beings, there will be the conditions for deliverance through pratyekabuddhas.

Even if hundreds of billions of Buddhas were to preach the Dharma for them, they would neither believe nor accept it; they can only attain liberation through the majestic deportment and the rules of conduct of pratyekabuddhas.

All these sentient beings collectively aspire to seek the path of a pratyekabuddha; yet at that time, no pratyekabuddhas appear in the world, so these sentient beings have no place where they may plant the causal conditions for roots of goodness.
At that time, for the sake of teaching and transforming beings, I personally declared myself to be a pratyekabuddha.
Throughout all the kingdoms, cities, towns, and villages, everyone knew that my body was that of a pratyekabuddha.
At that time, I manifested for all of them the physical form, color, and deportment of a pratyekabuddha; these sentient beings, with deep-seated reverence, all made offerings of food and drink to me.
After I had accepted the food, I observed the original causes and conditions regarding the Dharma they were to hear; having explained it for them, my body flew through the air like a king of geese.
At that time, all the sentient beings were filled with great joy and, with hearts of reverence, prostrated themselves before me with their heads at my feet, saying:
"May we, in future lives, all obtain the benefits of the Dharma just as this person has."
"Śāriputra! By these causes and conditions, I bring to fulfillment immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings, causing them to plant roots of goodness.
At that time, I observed that the multitude of people, having made offerings of food to me, were giving rise to feelings of weariness and distaste; I immediately addressed them, saying:"
"When the time for my parinirvāṇa has arrived," he said.
Upon hearing these words, hundreds of thousands of sentient beings each took flowers, incense, blended fragrances, and ghee-oil, and came to where I was.
At that time, I entered the meditative absorption of cessation (*nirodha-samāpatti*); yet, due to my original vow, I did not undergo ultimate extinction.
These sentient beings thought that my life had ended; because they wished to make offerings to me, they piled fragrant wood and cremated my body, believing that I had truly perished.
At that time, I again went to a great city in another country and declared of myself, "I am a Pratyekabuddha. The sentient beings therein also came to provide me with offerings of food and drink.
Within this [assembly], I manifest entry into nirvana, and they say, "He has passed away," whereupon they all come to make offerings and together cremate my body.
Thus it is, Śāriputra!
At that time, for the duration of one small kalpa—throughout three hundred and sixty billion lifetimes—I took the form of a pratyekabuddha and manifested entry into nirvana.
In every great city, I delivered and liberated thirty-six billion sentient beings by means of the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas.
“Śāriputra! In this way, the bodhisattva enters nirvāṇa by means of the pratyekabuddha vehicle, yet does not undergo ultimate extinction.

When Mañjuśrī spoke these words, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways and was pervaded with radiance. Ten billion devas made offerings to the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī, raining down celestial flowers, and all spoke these words:
"This is truly rare!

Today we have attained great and wholesome benefit, having seen the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī, and furthermore having heard this Śūraṅgama Samādhi being expounded."
“World-Honored One!
The Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī has accomplished such an unprecedented dharma; in what samādhi does he abide that he is able to manifest such an unprecedented dharma?”
The Buddha told the devas:
"The Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī, abiding in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, is able to perform such rare and difficult deeds."
When a bodhisattva dwells in this samādhi, they act as one who practices through faith, yet does not rely on the faith of others.
They also practice through the Dharma, turning the wheel of the Dharma within the characteristics of phenomena, neither regressing nor falling away.
He also manifests as one of the eight types of persons, practicing the Way for the sake of those who follow the eightfold wrong paths throughout immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.
He manifests as a *srotāpanna*, yet for the sake of sentient beings drifting in the waters of birth and death, he does not enter the fixed stage of the Dharma.
Acting as a Sakṛdāgāmin, they manifest their bodies throughout all worlds;
acting as an Anāgāmin, they likewise return to teach and transform sentient beings;
and acting as an Arhat, they also constantly apply themselves with diligence to seeking and studying the Buddha-dharma.
They also act as śrāvakas, preaching the Dharma to others with unimpeded eloquence.

They act as pratyekabuddhas, manifesting entry into nirvāṇa for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings through various causes and conditions; yet, by the power of samādhi, they return once more to birth.
"O sons of the gods!
When a bodhisattva abides in this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, they are able to universally practice all the deeds of the worthy ones and sages;
furthermore, they preach the Dharma according to their respective stages, yet they do not abide within them."
When the devas heard the Buddha speak these words, they all wept and said:
"World-Honored One!
If a person has already entered the stage of a śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha, they will forever lose this Śūraṅgama Samādhi."
World-Honored One!

A person would rather commit the five grave offenses of immediate retribution and hear this Śūraṅgama Samādhi being preached, than enter the stage of the Dharma and become an Arhat whose outflows are exhausted.

Why is this so? Because even those who have committed the five heinous crimes, having heard this Śūraṅgama Samādhi and resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, shall—though they fall into hell due to the conditions of their original sins—still attain Buddhahood by virtue of the roots of goodness resulting from hearing this samādhi.
"Bhagavān! An Arhat whose outflows are exhausted is like a broken vessel; he is forever incapable of receiving this samādhi. Bhagavān!"

For example, suppose there is a person who distributes ghee, oil, and honey, and a great multitude of people come with various vessels. Among them, one person is not firm in his attentiveness; he breaks the vessel he holds. Although he goes to the place where the ghee, oil, and honey are being distributed, he gains no benefit from it other than satisfying himself; he is unable to carry any back to give to others.
Among them, there was a person who possessed a vessel that was complete and sturdy; having satisfied himself, he also took a full vessel to bestow upon another.
The ghee, oil, and honey represent the Buddha’s True Dharma.
Those whose vessels are broken, who can only satisfy themselves but cannot carry them back to bestow upon others, are the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Those who hold complete vessels are the bodhisattvas; they not only satisfy themselves but are also able to carry [the vessel] to give to all sentient beings.

At that time, two hundred devaputras who had intended to turn back from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, having heard these words from the other devaputras and having heard of the inconceivable power of the merit of the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī, further resolved their hearts deeply toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. No longer following their previous inclination to regress, they all addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Even at the cost of harm to ourselves or the loss of our lives, we shall not abandon this resolve, nor shall we ever forsake any sentient being."
World-Honored One!
We only pray that by hearing the roots of goodness and causal conditions of this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, we shall attain the ten powers of a bodhisattva.
What are these ten?

They attain the power of firm resolve regarding the mind of enlightenment; the power of deep faith regarding the inconceivable Buddha-dharmas; the power of non-forgetfulness through extensive learning; the power of tirelessness in coming and going through birth and death; the power of steadfast great compassion toward all sentient beings; the power of firm relinquishment in the practice of giving; the power of indestructibility in the practice of ethical discipline; the power of steadfast endurance in the practice of patience; the power of wisdom that cannot be destroyed by Māra; and the power of faithful joy regarding all profound dharmas.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Resolute Mind:

"If there are sentient beings who, either now in the present or after my parinirvāṇa, hear of this Śūraṅgama Samādhi and are able to believe and rejoice in it, you should know that all such persons shall attain these ten powers of a bodhisattva."
At that time, there was a bodhisattva in the assembly named Mingyi (Nāman) who addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Those who wish to obtain merit should make offerings to the Buddha."
Those who wish to attain wisdom should be diligent in extensive learning;
those who wish to be born in a favorable realm should be diligent in maintaining ethical discipline;
those who wish for great wealth should increase their practice of giving.
Those who wish to attain a sublime physical form should cultivate patience;
those who wish to attain eloquence should respect their teachers and elders;
those who wish to attain dhāraṇīs should abandon overweening pride.
Those who wish to attain wisdom should cultivate right mindfulness;
those who wish to attain happiness should abandon all evil;
those who wish to benefit sentient beings should resolve to attain bodhicitta.
Those who wish to obtain a sublime voice should cultivate truthful speech;
those who wish to attain merit should delight in seclusion;
those who seek the Dharma should draw near to virtuous friends.
Those who wish to practice seated meditation should distance themselves from clamor and bustle;
those who wish to cultivate wisdom through reflection should practice contemplation;
those who wish to be reborn in the Brahma world should cultivate the immeasurable states of mind.
“World-Honored One! If one wishes to be born among devas or humans, one should cultivate the ten wholesome paths of action.
World-Honored One!

If there are those who wish to obtain merit, wish to obtain wisdom, wish to be born in a good place, wish for great wealth, wish for exquisite form, wish for eloquence, wish for *dhāraṇī*, wish to obtain knowledge, wish to obtain happiness, wish to benefit sentient beings, wish for a sublime voice, wish for merit, wish to seek the Dharma, wish to practice *dhyāna*, wish to attain the wisdom of reflection, wish to be born in the Brahma world, wish to be born among devas or humans, wish to attain *nirvāṇa*, or wish to obtain all merits—they should hear this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, receive, uphold, read, and recite it, explain it to others, and practice according to its teaching.”
“World-Honored One!
How should a bodhisattva cultivate this samādhi?
The Buddha said:

“O Mind! If a bodhisattva can contemplate the emptiness of all phenomena, remaining unobstructed, with every thought-moment ceasing and vanishing, and being free from hatred and attachment, this is called practicing this samādhi.”
Furthermore, O Mind!
One does not study this samādhi by means of a single thing. Why is that?
In accordance with the mental activities of all sentient beings, this samādhi possesses these various activities;
in accordance with the mental entries of all sentient beings, this samādhi possesses these various entries;
in accordance with the gateways of the faculties of all sentient beings, this samādhi possesses these gateways of entry.
According to the names and forms of all sentient beings, the bodhisattva who has attained this samādhi likewise manifests various names and forms;
to be able to know in this way is called the cultivation of this samādhi.
Just as all Buddhas manifest various names, forms, and appearances, the bodhisattva who has attained this samādhi likewise displays various names, forms, and appearances;
to be able to know it in this way is called cultivating this samādhi.
"Whichever Buddha-lands one beholds, the bodhisattva likewise spontaneously manifests as those very lands; this is called practicing this Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
The Bodhisattva named Arthamati addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One!"
"This samādhi is extremely difficult to cultivate.
The Buddha told Mingyi:
"For this reason, few bodhisattvas abide in this samādhi; many more bodhisattvas practice other samādhis."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Nāmanīti addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Bodhisattva Maitreya is in his last birth before Buddhahood; next after the World-Honored One, he shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
“Maitreya, has he attained this Śūraṅgama Samādhi? The Buddha said, “Nāman!”

"All those bodhisattvas who have attained the ten stages, those in their final birth before Buddhahood (ekajātipratibaddha), and those who have received the true position of a Buddha, have all attained this Śūraṅgama Samādhi.

At that moment, the Bodhisattva Maitreya manifested such supernatural power that the Bodhisattva Namati and the entire assembly saw that within every Jambudvīpa of this trichiliocosm, there was only the Bodhisattva Maitreya!
Some see him in the heavens;
some see him in the human world;
some see him as one who has left the household life.
Some see them as householders;
some see them attending upon the Buddha, all like Ānanda;
and some see them as foremost in wisdom, like Śāriputra.
Some see him as foremost in supernormal powers, like Maudgalyāyana;
some see him as foremost in ascetic practices, like Mahākāśyapa;
and some see him as foremost in preaching the Dharma, like Pūrṇa.
In some instances, he was seen as foremost in the observance of precepts, such as Rāhula;
in others, as foremost in the mastery of the Vinaya, such as Upāli;
and in others, as foremost in the divine eye, such as Aniruddha.
Or they may see him as foremost in seated meditation, like Revata;
in all such cases of being foremost among all, they shall see Maitreya!
Or they may see him entering various cities and villages to beg for food.
Some saw him preaching the Dharma;
others saw him sitting in meditation.

The Bodhisattva Mind-Name and the entire great assembly all beheld the miraculous power of Maitreya Bodhisattva’s manifestation of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi. Having seen this, they were filled with great joy and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Just as genuine gold does not lose its essential nature even when it is forged and polished, so too are these Great Beings;
wherever they are tested, they are all able to manifest the inconceivable dharma-nature.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Nāmanīti addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One!

I maintain that if a bodhisattva can penetrate the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, one should know that they have penetrated all paths of practice; they have fully penetrated the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, and the Great Vehicle of the Buddhas.”
The Buddha said: "So it is! So it is!"
"It is as you have said.
If a bodhisattva can penetrate the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, they will be able to penetrate all paths of practice.
At that time, the Elder Mahākāśyapa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

I believe that the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī has already performed the work of a Buddha in previous lives; he manifests sitting at the site of enlightenment, turns the wheel of the Dharma, and demonstrates to all sentient beings how to enter great parinirvāṇa.”
The Buddha said: “So it is! So it is!”
It is as you have said. Kāśyapa!

In the past, immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, there was a Buddha named Nāgottama Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.

To the south of this world, beyond a thousand Buddha-lands, there is a land named Samatā. It is devoid of mountains, rivers, sand, gravel, tiles, stones, hills, or mounds; the ground is as level as the palm of a hand and grows soft grass like that of Kalinga.

In that world, the Buddha Nāgottama attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and first turned the wheel of Dharma. He taught and brought to fulfillment seventy billion bodhisattvas; eight hundred million people became arhats; ninety-six thousand people dwelt in the causal conditions of the pratyekabuddha path; and thereafter there were immeasurable śrāvaka saṃghas.

Kāśyapa! The Buddha Superior Dragon-Lineage lived for four million four hundred thousand years. Having delivered devas and humans, he entered parinirvāṇa; his bodily relics were dispersed and spread throughout the world, and thirty-six billion stūpas were erected for sentient beings to make offerings to.
After that Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, the Dharma remained for one hundred thousand years.
When the Buddha Dragon-Species Superior (Nāgottama) was about to enter nirvāṇa, he conferred a prophecy upon the Bodhisattva Wisdom-Bright (Jñānaprabha), saying:
"This Bodhisattva Wisdom-Bright!"
"After me, he shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and his name shall also be Jñānaprabha.
Kāśyapa! Do you think that the Buddha Dragon-Supreme of the world Samatā at that time was anyone other than this person?
Do not give rise to such doubt.
Why is this? It is none other than Mañjuśrī, the Dharma Prince.

Kāśyapa! Behold now the power of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi! By means of this power, the great bodhisattvas manifest entering the womb, birth, renunciation, proceeding to the Bodhi tree, sitting at the site of enlightenment, turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma, entering parinirvāṇa, and distributing their relics; yet they do not abandon the qualities of a bodhisattva, and within parinirvāṇa, they do not undergo ultimate extinction.
At that time, the Elder Mahākāśyapa said to Mañjuśrī, “Virtuous one,
you are indeed able to perform such rare and difficult deeds, manifesting them for the sake of sentient beings.”
Mañjuśrī said: “Kāśyapa, what do you think?”
"By whom was this Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain created?
And from whence did this world emerge? Kāśyapa replied:
“Mañjuśrī! All worlds are composed of water-foam, and they likewise arise from the inconceivable karmic causes and conditions of sentient beings. Mañjuśrī said:
"All dharmas likewise arise from inconceivable karmic causes and conditions.
Regarding this matter, I possess no power or efficacy. Why is this so?..."
All phenomena are entirely dependent on causes and conditions; because they have no master, they are accomplished according to one's will.
If one can understand this, that which is undertaken will not be difficult.
Kāśyapa! If a person who has not yet seen the Four Truths can hear such matters and believe and understand them, this is indeed difficult.
But for one who has already seen the Four Truths and attained the various supernormal powers, it is not difficult to believe upon hearing this.

At that time, the World-Honored One ascended into the air to a height of seven tala trees and sat cross-legged; from his body issued forth a radiance that shone everywhere throughout immeasurable worlds in the ten directions.
The entire assembly all saw the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions, each of whom was preaching this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, neither increasing nor decreasing; they all heard it from afar.

The Buddhas of the ten directions also ascended into the void to a height of seven tala trees, sat cross-legged, and emitted light from their bodies that illuminated immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions.
Those sentient beings also saw the body of Śākyamuni Buddha ascend into the void and sit cross-legged.
All those in the assembly then took up flowers and scattered them from afar toward Śākyamuni Buddha!
Everyone saw the various flowers in the air above merging together to form flower canopies.

The bodhisattvas of this land, as well as the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others, all likewise scattered flowers upon those Buddhas, and these all transformed into flower canopies above the Buddhas.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha withdrew his supernormal powers and sat upon his original seat, addressing Dṛḍhamati, saying:
"This is the power of the Tathāgata’s supernormal penetrations; it is for the sake of increasing the merit of sentient beings that the Tathāgata has manifested this matter."
When the Buddha manifested his supernormal powers, eight thousand devas and humans resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Furthermore, as he was about to conclude his exposition of this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, the Bodhisattva Resolute Mind (*Dṛḍhamati*) and five hundred bodhisattvas attained the Śūraṅgama Samādhi. They all beheld the supernatural powers of all the Buddhas of the ten directions, obtained the light of wisdom regarding the profound Dharma of the Buddhas, dwelt in the tenth stage, and received their stations as successors to the Buddhas.

The trichiliocosm shook in six ways, emitting a great radiance that illuminated the entire world; ten million musical instruments played simultaneously, and the devas in the heavens rained down various kinds of flowers.
At that time, the Buddha told Ānanda:
"You should receive this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, uphold, recite, and read it, and explain it extensively for others.
Then, the Śakra who holds the summit of Mount Sumeru addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Ānanda’s wisdom and mindfulness are limited; as a śrāvaka, he follows the voices of others. For what reason do you entrust this Dharma-treasure of samādhi to Ānanda?”
Śakra, holding the summit of Mount Sumeru, spoke these words of sincere resolve:

"If it be true that I shall, in this life and in future lives, widely proclaim and disseminate this Jewel Samādhi without fail, then let all the trees on this Vulture Peak Mountain become like the Bodhi tree of the Buddha, and beneath each of those trees, may there be a bodhisattva."
After Śakra, who dwells upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, had spoken these words, he immediately saw all the trees as being like the Bodhi tree; beneath each and every tree, he beheld a Bodhisattva.
All the Bodhi trees spoke these words:
"As Śakra, who dwells on the summit of Mount Sumeru, has spoken, so shall it be; this person will surely cause this samādhi to be widely proclaimed and disseminated."
At that time, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others, with one voice, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Even if the Tathāgata were to remain for the duration of a kalpa and, for no other purpose, preach the Dharma to people using the Śrāvaka vehicle, such that each instance of preaching resulted in the salvation of as many sentient beings as were saved at the first turning of the Wheel of Dharma—nevertheless, the number of sentient beings saved by preaching this Śūraṅgama Samādhi would be superior.”
