Why is this? Because all these sentient beings are delivered by means of the Śrāvaka-yāna; compared to the Bodhisattva-yāna, they do not equal even one hundredth part, nor one thousandth, ten-thousandth, or hundred-thousand-millionth part, nor can they be reached even by calculation or analogy.
"Such is the Śūraṅgama Samādhi; it possesses such immeasurable power that it can bring all bodhisattvas to fulfillment, enabling them to be complete in the Buddha-dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Resolute Mind addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, what is your actual lifespan?"
"At what time shall you enter ultimate nirvana?
The Buddha said, "Dṛḍhamati!"

To the east, thirty-two thousand buddha-fields away from this world, there is a land named Adorned. In it dwells a Buddha, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, named Illuminating Adornment Sovereign King (Prabhāsa-vyūheśvararāja), who currently resides there preaching the Dharma.
“Dṛḍhamati! Just as is the lifespan of the Buddha Prabhāsa-alaṃkāra-vibhūti-rāja, so too is my own lifespan!
“World-Honored One!”
"How long is the lifespan of that Buddha Prabhāsa-vyūha-vaśavartin?
The Buddha told Dṛḍhamati:
"Go ask him yourself; he will surely answer you."

Immediately, Resolute Mind (Dṛḍhamati), sustained by the Buddha’s spiritual power, and further empowered by the force of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi as well as his own roots of goodness and supernormal powers, reached that World of Adornment in the space of a single thought-moment.
He prostrated with his head at the feet of that Buddha, circumambulated him three times to the right, and standing to one side, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, how long will your lifespan last?
When will you enter parinirvāṇa?"
That Buddha replied:
"Just as the lifespan of that Śākyamuni Buddha is, so too is my lifespan! Vīradatta!"
"If you wish to know, my lifespan shall be seven hundred *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, and the lifespan of Śākyamuni Buddha shall likewise be so!
At that time, the Bodhisattva Resolute Mind was filled with great joy; he immediately returned to the Sahā world and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
That Buddha, King of Sovereign Radiance and Adornment, had a lifespan of seven hundred asaṃkhyeya kalpas.
He addressed me, saying:
"As is my lifespan, so too is the lifespan of Śākyamuni Buddha!"
At that time, Ānanda rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has taught, I believe that the World-Honored One benefits sentient beings in that Adorned World under a different name."
At that time, the World-Honored One praised Ānanda, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
By the power of the Buddha, you are able to know this matter:
that Buddha’s body is my own body; under a different name, I preach the Dharma there to deliver and liberate sentient beings.
"Ānanda! Such powers of mastery over supernormal faculties are all due to the power of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Resolute Mind:
“Dṛḍhamati! For this reason, you should know that my lifespan shall last for seven hundred asaṃkhyeya kalpas before I finally enter parinirvāṇa.

When the great assembly heard what the Buddha had said—that his lifespan was thus inconceivable—they were all filled with great joy at such an unprecedented occurrence and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The spiritual power of all Buddhas is unprecedented; all their deeds are inconceivable. Although they manifest such a short lifespan here, in reality it spans seven hundred *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.”
“World-Honored One!
May all sentient beings be endowed with such inconceivable life spans.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed Resolute Mind:

"Wherever this Śūraṅgama Samādhi resides—whether in a commandery, a kingdom, a city, a town, a village, a monastery, or a forest—none of the Māras or their followers shall find any opportunity there."
He further addressed Dṛḍhamati:

"If there is a Dharma master who copies, recites, and explains this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, they shall have no fear of humans or non-humans, and shall furthermore attain twenty parts of inconceivable merit."
What are the twenty inconceivable merits?
His wisdom is inconceivable; his insight is inconceivable; his skillful means are inconceivable;
his eloquence is inconceivable; his illumination of the Dharma is inconceivable; his dhāraṇīs are inconceivable.
The Dharma-gates are inconceivable; mindfulness according to their meaning is inconceivable;
the various supernormal powers are inconceivable; the discernment of the various languages of sentient beings is inconceivable;
the profound understanding of the inclinations of the minds of sentient beings is inconceivable; and the attainment of the vision of all Buddhas is inconceivable.
The deliberation [concerns that] the various dharmas heard are inconceivable; the teaching and transformation of sentient beings are inconceivable;
the sovereign samādhis are inconceivable; the accomplishment of the pure land is inconceivable;
the most wondrous physical form is inconceivable; the sovereignty of merit is inconceivable; and the cultivation and purification of the various *pāramitās*...
The perfection of wisdom is inconceivable; the attainment of non-retrogression in the Buddha-dharma is inconceivable.
These are the twenty. "Firm Mind!..."
If a person copies, reads, or recites this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, they shall obtain a share of these twenty inconceivable merits.
Therefore, Resolute Mind!
"If anyone wishes to obtain all benefits in this life and future lives, they should copy, read, recite, explain, and practice this Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
Resolute Mind!..."

If good sons or good daughters seeking the Buddha-way diligently practice the six *pāramitās* with a devoted mind for thousands of millions of kalpas, yet if there are those who, upon hearing this Śūraṅgama Samādhi, are able to believe and accept it, their minds neither regressing nor sinking, and they are neither startled nor afraid—their merit shall surpass that of the former, and they will swiftly reach *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
How much more so if, having heard it, they uphold, recite, and study it, practice according to the teaching, and explain it to others?

If there are bodhisattvas who wish to hear the inconceivable Dharma of all Buddhas without being startled or terrified, and who wish to realize and know it for themselves within the teachings of all Buddhas without relying on the instruction of others, they should cultivate and practice this samādhi.
If they wish to hear the Dharma never heard before and accept it with faith without opposition, they should listen to this Śūraṅgama Samādhi.

When this Śūraṅgama Samādhi Sūtra was being spoken, immeasurable sentient beings resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; twice that number established themselves on the stage of avaivartika;
and twice that number again attained the endurance of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
Eighteen thousand bodhisattvas attained this Śūraṅgama Samādhi;
eighteen thousand bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, because they did not grasp at any dharmas, were liberated through the exhaustion of outflows and attained arhatship.
Twenty-six thousand upāsakas and upāsikās attained the pure Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena;
thirty nayutas of devas entered the stage of the noble ones.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra,

Mañjuśrī the Dharma Prince, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Resolute Mind, and all the other Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas, as well as the great śrāvaka disciples, and all the world’s inhabitants— including devas, nāgas, spirits, gandharvas, asuras, and others— having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and faithfully accepted it.
The Scripture on the Śūraṅgama Samādhi Spoken by the Buddha, Volume II.
